note: BUMPED to 1.0.8 from 1.0.7. THE TRANSCRIPTION, THE SECTION MODEL AND THE ANCHORS ARE UNCHANGED: source.txt is byte-identical to 1.0.7’s (sha256 748e58cef10981193585a101fcf67951cc3a37577eaf756f08399e343e1dd8bf), divisions.json and base.json are carried unchanged, and the new pin tools/anchors/proclus-theology-of-plato-taylor-1816@1.0.8.json is byte-identical to 1.0.7’s (anchorHash 41341b7e…) — NOT ONE CITATION ANCHOR MOVES. SIX RULES MOVE: all six are `transliteration` rules whose `transliteration` class the 1.0.4 witness pass cleared from `review` and whose readings had never been read off the page by an instrument shown no candidate text. FOUR OF THE SIX READINGS ARE CORRECTED, and because a corrected reading may not be written beneath a spent id, their four ids are WITHDRAWN and the corrected rules are APPENDED as r11895–r11898 (the id sequence keeps its gaps, and the gap IS the record): r11693 served `φάρσχε πρῶ … τὰς δευτερείας τιμᾶσ`, where `φάρσχε` is not a Greek word, and now serves the print’s `δευτέρας τιμάς … τὰς προσηκούσας τιμάς`; r11707 served the five Valentinian æones in the WRONG ORDER (`σιγη, βυθος, νους`) where the print sets `νοῦς, βύθος, σιγή, ἀλήθεια, σοφία`; r11812 served `ορουμ and θεῖα` where the print sets `ὀρούω and θείω` — both of the rule’s words ended in the wrong letter while the print’s own sentence on the same line says the letter in question “is here an ω”; and r11705’s reading was right except for one impossible character (U+0302 COMBINING CIRCUMFLEX ACCENT over an epsilon, which Greek cannot set). TWO ARE UPHELD on a blind read of their own page (r11709, r11719) and are re-flagged in place, each with a witness entry recording the read that put it back on the worklist. ALL SIX NOW STAND FLAGGED FOR REVIEW, which is what their class requires — one instrument’s reading, the class re-derived from the draw cache and not read off any note. WHY THE FLAGS WERE CLEARED AND WHY THAT CANNOT STAND: the witness locator’s token stream is ASCII letters and digits ONLY, so for a transliteration rule its “the witness carries the rule’s whole `after` reading” test is decided on the English AROUND the Greek, and the Greek the rule exists to supply is never compared — these rules were cleared by a test blind to the characters they supply. TWO EVIDENCE LEAVES ARE CORRECTED with the readings they carry (r11693 n23→n22, r11707 n18→n17), MEASURED by blind reads of both leaves on each. THE GATE `tools/echo-probe.mjs` HAS BEEN RED AT 1.0.4, 1.0.5, 1.0.6 AND 1.0.7 (68 OK, 1 FAIL, naming r11693) AND IS GREEN HERE BY THE SAME ASSERTION, NOT BY A RELAXATION: the assertion still holds every single-instrument merged rule to `review: true`, no expectation in the probe was touched, and on a fixture whose flag is removed again it goes red naming the rule. NOTHING ELSE MOVES: 3,255 rules (1.0.7: 3,255), no OCR or punctuation rule touched, not one served English word changed, and every rule still fires. This edition also now has ONE gate runner (`tools/gates.mjs`), which enumerates every gate in the repository from the directory and prints each one’s exit code, so a red gate cannot be invisible again.
citation: Proclus, On the Theology of Plato, trans. Thomas Taylor (London, 1816). The Neoplatonic Library, version 1.0.8. https://neoplatonic-library.org/texts/proclus-theology-of-plato-taylor-1816/
